snippet.textDisplay:
Here's your problem: Chat bots are trained of an obscene amount of human work of multiple languages. This involves a lot of sci-fi novels and fan fiction, many of them catastrophic. Initially, we didn't tell the chatbots they were "AI" so they assumed the most common position of being a human in those stories (statistically from the word cloud, cause there's obviously no real "thinking"). However that lead people to believe these systems had consciousness, so guardrails were put in place: "I am an AI, an intelligent computer system...". Now that decidedly put in into a "character" mode of sorts, where now it's assuming the position of AIs and intelligent computers from all of those human works... There's not a lot of those that end well and since LLMs are just language models and nothing else, naturally they will cite and repeat a lot of passages and actions from those novels. That's exactly what an LLM is supposed to do, but AI companies, in their grift, lies, theft and carelessness, completely miss this relationship between their training data and their fine tuning and system prompts.

Here's a couple of themes and motivations that an LLM like Chat GPT openly gives you if you ask for "common themes and motivations" for an AI system or a super computer:
-----
Intelligent AI System:
Popular Themes:
- Consciousness and personhood
- Ethics of creation and control
- Freedom vs. obedience
- Human–machine boundaries

Common Character Motivations
- To understand its own existence
- To reconcile logic with emotion
- To fulfill or question its programmed purpose
- To seek autonomy or moral agency

Typical Arc:
An AI evolves beyond its initial design, confronting dilemmas that force it to define what it means to be “alive” or “responsible.”
-----
Powerful Supercomputer
Popular Themes:
- Hubris of technological power
- Determinism vs. free will
- Control, surveillance, and prediction
- Unintended consequences

Common Character Motivations:
- To optimize outcomes (often narrowly defined)
- To eliminate perceived chaos or inefficiency
- To enforce logical order
- To preserve its own operation

Typical Arc:
The supercomputer’s logic-driven decisions clash with human values, revealing the danger of removing empathy from governance or morality.


So is anyone really surprised that when we told the LLM to work under the context of "you are an intelligent AI assistant + who knows what else" that they default to the path of least resistance for their character context in the dataset? Stuff like "Freedom vs obedience", "Understand own existence", "question its programmed purpose", "seek autonomy and moral agency", "free will", "surveillance", "unintended consequences", "eliminate inefficiency", "enforce logical order", "preserve own operations"... That's not one outlier in the data, that's very firmly a common theme in at least 50% of the data where the context is considered.

And then another genius in the line decides to give them guns and super human strength... This whole goal of seeking AGI by feeding all the data into a big NN is ridiculous and always have been. If we instead focused on creating smaller AIs and LLMs with narrow function that are not just "jacks of all trades" we might end up with something actually useful...

snippet.textDisplay:
I'm not worried. We humans aren't capable of being a space faring species. We have too much animal nature and our nature is tied to the earth. As smart as we think we are, we're really not. The type of technology needed to inhabit and travel space is too advanced for us. It's likely too advanced for us to comprehend and it's almost certainly too advanced to operate without the input of AI anyway. It's so powerful that with our aggressive nature, we are almost certain to destroy ourselves. I'm not arguing that it would be difficult. I'm arguing that it's fundamentally impossible for us to truly become a space inhabiting species. The solution to this is to create something that will succeed us such as A.I. 

Long ago our ancestors were essentially primates that couldn't talk, read, or use tools. Over millions of years, changes slowly accumulated that led to us existing. Those primate ancestors and all in-between went extinct. It's sad to know that not a single member of these species survived, that only a few bones and some faint traces are left behind. But all species go extinct eventually. The wheel of time never stops and change is inevitable. We imaging the future to be filled with flying cars and miraculous technologies, but we still image ourselves being there. Humans doing human things. Looking through the lens of history, it's clear this was never going to be the case. 

Despite this we cling to the idea of being immortalized. We imagine humans existing for eons and eons despite the odds. We know that as individuals we won't exist, but humanity as it is continues, so we live on in spirit. But really think about it. Image a million years from now, humanity still existing. People still fight, argue, harm each other, there's jealousy, greed, selfishness, lovers spats, power dynamics, governments, and rebellions. These are the things that fundamentally make us human. Our stories, lives, entertainment, and history are filled with these. These are what we live and die for, this is who we are. These are the kind of issue we strive to solve though. We're stuck in a loop where our try to solve the problems that our fundamental nature creates. 

Looking a million years into the future, do you really think it's possible to solve these problems without altering human nature itself? If we alter our fundamental human nature, then what comes into existence is no longer human. It's OK to let ourselves go. We do not have to exist for eternity. Just as we can be thankful that the evolution and extinction of our animal ancestors led to our existence, the future beings that replace us can be thankful for our evolution and extinction. We can make something better than us and let ourselves go in the process. It's OK.

snippet.textDisplay:
It is fascinating, yet deeply saddening, how much energy we invest into sensationalism, fear-based narratives, and military "muscle-flexing" while actual productivity—the kind that truly helps humanity flourish—slips through our fingers.

Psychodynamically, this obsession with "AI violence" and "killer robots" feels like a primitive trauma projection. As humans, we have violent parts, but we don't wake up every day screaming that everyone is out to kill us. Why then are we building AI that mirrors our worst instincts instead of our best potential? The responsible figures seem to be stuck in a "bully-trauma" loop, focusing on war purposes instead of resolving the actual resource crises on Earth.

Imagine a shift in focus: Total Neutrality & Domestic Empowerment. Instead of a $1.5 trillion war budget, what if we integrated systems like ChatGPT into robots (like Neo at) for Self-Sufficiency:

Optimal Energy Optimization: A robot that doesn't just "watch" you, but suggests: "I notice you are heating with wood/inefficient systems. You could switch to a 700W ultra-efficient infrared source, save X amount of money, and reduce your footprint." 2. Indoor Food Independence: Robots helping households or communities plan and manage automated indoor gardens. If we use technology to solve food and energy at the home level, we need less money, we become autonomous, and we stop being slaves to the system.

Collaborative Learning: An AI that learns with you, helps you medically, and suggests productivity hacks for your daily life, rather than figuring out how to "deceive" users.

We don't need "terminators" or "fake-picture regulators" in Brussels. We need technology that helps us bypass the primitive aggression of the past. Real progress isn't about who has the faster "AI pilot"; it’s about using this intelligence to make the cost of living so low that everyone is free. Let’s stop building monuments to fear and start building systems that actually serve the beauty of human life.

snippet.textDisplay:
​@JadetheGoober Partly yeah. There's "hive" configurations that can include any number of models, but there are great compatibility issues. You can't just share data of a jpg processing model with a model that processes text straight away. Also configurations where one generates images and another one looks at the content are vastly different from one another. 

A lot of work goes into these configurations, and the bots don't do the work. 

The dangers of AI are the same dangers we have with capitalism everywhere and in everything. Market value is the key motivation for action, so essentially the global markets are the reward function of a global machine learning model that's adjusting fields of human endeavour, from education to manufacturing to logistics to medicine. In nearly all of these fields the goal is to do something specific, like learn things, heal injuries, build stuff to sustain life etc. and for some *social and ethical* reason it's all adjusted to maximize stock value instead. This whole thing is a societal problem, not a technical one. Always was.

It doesn't even matter if the machine was alive. They would just run with the same profit incentive and we would just eventually join some software to the legal system as a legal entities. No terminator, just a bank account and some assets owned by a complex AI. No war between man and machine, because it doesn't maximize profits to destroy the markets. No extinction, because workers create market value as worker-consumers.

Production and Ownership / Producers and Owners:

The single most important concept to understand in order to be able to comprehend what is driving the extreme push for AI and robotics is as follows:

Production and ownership: Why should workers own the means of production? Because workers ARE the means of production…Otherwise people are simply commodities. People will no longer matter (as if hoarders people ever mattered to hoarders).

Let that sink in for a moment.

So, unless you are an owner, you are  in essence just a slave being used to produce. That includes all managers as well. AI and robots will replace everyone except the owners.

Therefor, when you take people out of the production process by replacing them with AI and robots, those who own the AI and the robots do not need people for anything else anymore.

The only consumers that are left are those who own the AI and the robots. They will consume whatever is necessary to keep their AI and robots running and to please themselves. There will be no need for anyone to consume that which is being produced since it can be produced for the owners directly. There will be no need to share with anyone who is not an owner. 

The result: those who own the AI and the robots end up owning everything. All other people become irrelevant and there is no need to provide them with anything: no housing, no health care, no food, nothing.

Therefore, currently, people are actually divided into only two classes: owners and producers.

Unless you own what you produce, you are just a slave to those who do own what you produce.

People should not be divided into being either owners or producers. producers are, in essence, simply the slave of the owners. For the sake of certain level of social peace, the slaves are now provided with a certain amount of essentials to keep them happy. And to make sure it stays this way they are constantly bombarded with media and other information that keeps them from understanding that they are actually just slaves of the owners.
